_note: Source for DSS dataset and column descriptions. Feature-column wording is NOT here: webapp/backend/feature_glossary.py is the single copy and tools/push_descriptions.py reads it at push time. Apply with tools/push_descriptions.py --push.

columns.disease_index: MONDO disease node index from graph_nodes. The join key for every per-disease table -- an internal integer, not a MONDO CURIE.
columns.gene_index: Gene/protein node index from graph_nodes. Pairs with disease_index to key one candidate.
columns.disease: Human-readable disease label. Display only -- join on disease_index.
columns.disease_name: Human-readable disease label. Display only -- join on disease_index.
columns.gene: HGNC gene symbol. Display only -- join on gene_index.
columns.gene_name: HGNC gene symbol. Display only -- join on gene_index.
columns.node_id: Source-native identifier as it arrived (MONDO CURIE, Entrez id, ChEMBL id, ...). Display and provenance; join on node_index.
columns.node_group: Node type bucket used by the graph webapp's grouping (protein, disease, drug, pathway, effect, ...).
columns.relation: Edge relation type, one of the graph's 18 relations.
columns.display_relation: Relation label for display; several raw relations collapse to one display label.
columns.count: Row count for the grouping this table aggregates over.
columns.n_genes: Number of distinct genes in this row's scope.
columns.n_known: Number of already-annotated known targets in this row's scope.
columns.n_known_targets: Number of curated known targets for this disease.
columns.disease_family_id: Disease family the grouped split groups on. Terms in the same family never straddle train/test.
columns.disease_split_key: The grouped-split key. Zero straddling keys is what makes every held-out number mean anything.
columns.split_key_rule: Which rule assigned this split key -- the audit trail for the leakage control.
columns.anchor_name: The family anchor term this split key was derived from.
columns.hop_depth: Hops from the family anchor in the MONDO hierarchy. Act 3's ontology indentation is this column drawn.
columns.split: Train / validation / test membership, assigned by disease_split_key rather than by row.
columns.is_target: Label: 1 when the gene is an annotated target for this disease. NEVER a model input.
columns.proba_1: Champion m7-f14 predicted probability that the pair is a target.
columns.prediction: Thresholded class from the champion. The ranking, not this flag, is what the demo shows.
columns.score: Champion score used for ranking within a disease.
columns.rank: Rank within the disease pool, 1 = highest scoring.
columns.rank_in_disease: Rank within this disease's candidate pool, 1 = highest scoring.
columns.rank_in_subtype: Rank within the subtype's candidate pool, 1 = highest scoring.
columns.rank_percentile: Percentile position within the disease pool.
columns.target_rank_sum: Sum of known-target ranks; lower is better. Used to compare rankings without a threshold.
columns.auc_disease: Per-disease AUROC on held-out data. Aggregate as a MACRO mean across diseases; a pooled AUC is a different and wrong number.
columns.auc_lo95: Lower bound of the Hanley-McNeil 95% interval for auc_disease.
columns.auc_hi95: Upper bound of the Hanley-McNeil 95% interval for auc_disease.
columns.auc_trustworthy: Whether this disease has enough positives for its AUC to carry weight. Filter on it before quoting a per-disease number.
columns.auc_drug_targets: AUROC against curated drug-target labels instead of association labels -- the therapeutic axis. A warning signal, never an optimisation target.
columns.auc_assoc_labels: AUROC against the association labels, for comparison with auc_drug_targets.
columns.n_pos: Positives in this disease's held-out pool.
columns.n_neg: Negatives in this disease's held-out pool.
columns.hits_at_10: Known targets recovered in the top 10.
columns.hits_at_20: Known targets recovered in the top 20.
columns.hits_at_50: Known targets recovered in the top 50.
columns.recall_at_20: Share of this disease's known targets recovered in the top 20.
columns.rank_enrichment: How much higher known targets rank than chance for this disease.
columns.enrichment_at_50: Enrichment of known targets in the top 50 over the pool base rate.
columns.module_size: Protein seeds annotated for the disease. A property of the DISEASE, not the pair, and NOT a champion input.
columns.dwpc_GCD: Degree-weighted paths reaching the disease through a shared drug. NOT a champion input -- retained for the ablation record.
columns.gene_n_diseases: How many diseases the gene is already annotated for. NOT a champion input: alone it scores 0.8567 AUC, which measures gene popularity rather than biology.
columns.degree: Gene degree in the graph, independent of any disease. NOT a champion input.
columns.pagerank: Gene PageRank, independent of any disease. NOT a champion input.
columns.eigenvector_centrality: Gene eigenvector centrality, independent of any disease. NOT a champion input.
columns.triangles: Triangle count around the gene. NOT a champion input.
columns.clustering_coefficient: Local clustering coefficient of the gene. NOT a champion input.
columns.ppi_common_neighbors: Raw count of interaction partners shared with the disease module. NOT a champion input -- the champion uses the degree-corrected z-score ppi_common_neighbors_z instead.
columns.ppi_cn_expected: Shared partners that gene degree alone predicts; the baseline ppi_common_neighbors_z is measured against.
columns.ppi_edges_with_provenance: Interactions carrying at least one named source; the denominator behind the provenance features.
columns.rwr_score: Random-walk-with-restart proximity to the disease module. NOT a champion input.
columns.rwr_norm: Normalised rwr_score. NOT a champion input.
columns.prox_mean: Mean hop distance to the disease module; companion to prox_closest. NOT a champion input.
columns.prox_n_reach: How many module genes are reachable at all; the denominator prox_mean is computed over.
columns.shared_pathway_count: Raw count of pathways shared with the disease module; the champion uses the fraction (shared_pathway_frac) instead.
columns.disease_context: Disease-side context feature. NOT a champion input.
columns.has_inflammatory_go_annotation: Whether the gene carries an inflammatory GO annotation. NOT a champion input.
columns.druggability_class: Open Targets tractability bucket. Display annotation and a filter the scientist sets -- never a model input.
columns.safety_flag: Public safety-liability flag. Display only: the discovery lift is measured against exactly these labels, so filtering on it makes the headline claim circular.
columns.localization_class: Subcellular localisation bucket, from the GO hierarchy. Display annotation only.
columns.lof_intolerant: Loss-of-function intolerance flag. Display annotation only.
columns.ground_truth: Which label set this row is scored against (approved / investigational / curated).
columns.act3_family: Which act 3 family this term belongs to.
columns.subtype: Subtype term within the family. Subtype means something different per family -- biomarker for breast, histological for lung.
columns.pool: Candidate pool the row was drawn from.
columns.pool_size: Size of the candidate pool for this disease.
columns.disease_pool_size: Number of scored candidates for this disease.
columns.is_eligible: Whether the disease passes the seed gate. Only 1,157 of 27,153 disease nodes do; the 95.7% excluded is the study's central limit.
columns.node_index: Internal integer node identity. THIS is what every edge and feature table joins on, not node_id.
columns.node_type: One of the graph's 8 node types: protein, disease, drug, pathway, effect/phenotype, biological_process, molecular_function, cellular_component.
columns.node_name: Human-readable label for the node. Display only.
columns.node_source: Which source system the node came from. Six are external; MONDO_grouped is ours, and saying so is part of act 1's honesty.
columns.in_act3: Whether this term appears in act 3's family panel.
columns.act3_role: The term's role inside its family: the family anchor, or one of its subtypes.
columns.in_act4: Whether this disease appears in act 4's disease picker.
columns.act4_area: Therapeutic area label act 4 groups the singleton diseases under.
columns.act4_order: Display order in act 4's disease picker.
columns.top_shap_drivers: The candidate's strongest SHAP contributions, precomputed for the detail card. Explanation, not a score.
columns.ot_class_l1: Open Targets top-level target class. Display annotation only.
columns.ot_sm_tractable: Small-molecule tractability flag from Open Targets. Display annotation and a user-set filter, never a model input.
columns.ot_ab_tractable: Antibody tractability flag from Open Targets. Display annotation and a user-set filter, never a model input.
columns.has_approved_drug: Whether any approved drug hits this gene, for any disease. A badge, not a filter -- the discovery lift is measured against this label.
columns.approved_for_disease: Whether an approved drug links this gene to THIS disease. This is the label act 4's lift is measured against, so it must never become a filter.
columns.investigational_for_disease: Whether an investigational drug links this gene to this disease. Same rule as approved_for_disease.
columns.has_safety_liability: Whether the gene carries any public safety flag. Display only; filtering on it deletes ERBB2 from its own disease's list.
columns.n_safety_liabilities: How many distinct safety flags the gene carries. Display only.
columns.safety_events: Reported adverse-event categories for the gene. Display only -- this is not a toxicity assessment.
columns.safety_dosing: Dosing-related safety notes for the gene. Display only.
columns.lof_oe: Observed/expected loss-of-function ratio; lower means more intolerant to loss of function.
columns.lof_oe_upper: Upper confidence bound on lof_oe; the bound, not the point estimate, is what constraint claims should use.
columns.mis_oe: Observed/expected missense ratio for the gene.
columns.datatypes: Which evidence datatypes back the disease-gene labels, and in what proportion -- the definition of "known target".
columns.feature: Feature column name this row reports on.

graph_node_type_counts.short: Act 1: node count per type across the assembled graph. Read whole at webapp startup and cached.

graph_node_source_counts.short: Act 1: node count per source. Six sources are external; MONDO_grouped is ours, which is the one to say out loud.

graph_relation_counts.short: Act 1: edge count for each of the graph's 18 relations.

graph_ppi_provenance.short: Act 1: how many interaction edges are corroborated by one, two or more interactomes.
graph_ppi_provenance.long: This is the table act 1's provenance chart is built from, and it pays off later: the champion's two strongest SHAP drivers are ppi_evidence_depth and ppi_multi_source_frac, both derived from this same corroboration signal.

graph_label_evidence.short: Act 1: the disease-gene evidence split that defines what "known target" means.
graph_label_evidence.long: The act's honesty depends on this table. "Known target" is a curated label with a provenance mix, not a fact, and this is where that mix is shown.

disease_eligibility.short: Act 2: the seed-gate funnel, 27,153 disease nodes down to 1,157 eligible.
disease_eligibility.long: The 95.7% this gate excludes is the study's central limit and the demo says so explicitly. A disease with too few annotated seeds cannot be scored or evaluated, so it never enters the population.

validation_auc_by_disease.short: Act 2: per-disease held-out AUROC with Hanley-McNeil confidence intervals, for all 670 validation diseases.
validation_auc_by_disease.long: Read THIS dataset, not validation_auc_by_disease_2 -- the _2 variant is a two-level table nothing reads. Aggregate as a macro mean across diseases; a pooled AUC is a different and wrong number.

validation_auc_ci.short: Intermediate: per-disease AUC with its interval, feeding family_panel in A3.

hub_bias_meter.short: Act 2: whether the model under-scores poorly connected true targets, with biology held constant.
hub_bias_meter.long: This is the detection question, and it is deliberately measured twice: nb3 asks whether the top 50 over-samples high-degree genes (about the ranking), nb3b asks this (about detection). They point opposite ways and both are true.

orthogonality_scatter.short: Act 2: per-disease association AUC against drug-target-benchmark AUC.
orthogonality_scatter.long: The point of the scatter is that the two axes are only loosely related. A high association AUC does not buy therapeutic relevance, which is why the drug benchmark is reported as a warning rather than optimised.

drug_target_benchmark.short: Per-disease AUROC scored against curated drug-target labels instead of association labels.
drug_target_benchmark.long: Treat as a WARNING signal, never an optimisation target: this benchmark can measure gene popularity rather than model quality.

novel_discovery_eval.short: Discovery lift on genes the labels do not already claim, by ground-truth class and rank cutoff.
novel_discovery_eval.long: This is the closest thing the project has to a discovery claim, and it is deliberately modest -- the ranked list beats chance on not-yet-annotated genes, which is not the same as finding something new.

persona_enrichment.short: Per-disease enrichment used to pick the demo panel and to render act 3's spread.

persona_candidates.short: Candidate diseases considered for the demo panel, with the metrics the choice was made on.

split_audit_2.short: Act 2: proof that no disease split key straddles train, validation or test.
split_audit_2.long: Zero straddling keys is the claim every held-out number rests on. Its recipe once failed silently for weeks, leaving the leakage guarantee unverified -- which is why this table is shown rather than asserted.

family_validation_scored.short: Intermediate: champion scores joined to family membership, first step of the per-family AUC chain.

family_validation_ranked.short: Intermediate: per-family ranking, second step of the per-family AUC chain.

family_auc_grouped.short: Intermediate: per-family aggregation, third step of the per-family AUC chain.

family_auc_by_family.short: Per-therapeutic-area AUC, the endpoint of the family AUC chain. Read by the webapp and by nb3.
family_auc_by_family.long: Moved from zone 90 to A2 on 2026-09-03 because the webapp reads it -- it is serving data, not notebook staging.

demo_panel_config.short: Which families and diseases the demo carries. Changing this repoints act 3 and, through validation_set_personas_2, the whole candidate chain.
demo_panel_config.long: Read docs/demo/panel_selection.html before repointing it. The panel was measured over all 670 validation diseases: subtype structure exists only in oncology, so act 3 is breast plus uterine and therapeutic-area breadth comes from act 4's singletons.

family_panel.short: Family panel with hop depth, the ontology skeleton act 3 indents.

family_panel_metrics.short: Act 3: per-subtype AUC with its interval and known-target count, for every term in the panel.

family_panel_top50.short: Act 3: the gene-by-term top-50 rank matrix. Covers every term in the config, not just the persona diseases.
family_panel_top50.long: It replaced top50_membership, which held only the persona diseases and made the matrix look like a subset of itself.

family_panel_overlap.short: Act 3: pairwise top-50 overlap between terms, with the ontology gap between them.
family_panel_overlap.long: This is the table that decides whether a family's subtypes are really distinguishable. Breast subtypes share only about 4% of their top-50 novel candidates; lung histological subtypes do not separate at all.

family_panel_programme.short: Act 3: which candidates are common to a family versus specific to one subtype.

dashboard_candidates.short: Act 4: the ranked candidate table the scientist filters. The only dataset with a per-request WHERE and the only Snowflake candidate.
dashboard_candidates.long: Everything else in the serving zones is read whole and cached; this one is queried per disease. The drug badges and the liability flag on it are display-only and must never become filters, because the discovery lift is measured against exactly those labels.

filter_three_axes.short: Act 4: the three-axis filter counts -- novel, tractable, and free of known liabilities.

known_drug_truth.short: Curated drug-target ground truth used to score the shortlist.

shap_driver_frequency.short: Act 2: how often each feature is a top SHAP driver, standing in for feature importance.
shap_driver_frequency.long: Lives in zone 40 beside the scored table it is computed from, not in A2 where it is displayed. It is a frequency over the scoring output, not a global importance.

shap_drivers_long.short: Intermediate: per-candidate SHAP drivers in long form, feeding shap_driver_frequency.

breast_panel_metrics.short: Breast subtype panel built to be falsified by a breast surgeon rather than by our own labels.
breast_panel_metrics.long: A surgeon can falsify a candidate list in minutes, which is a harder test than any metric in the document. The risk measured first was whether breast subtypes resolve at all: they do, sharing only ~4% of their top-50 novel candidates, unlike lung histological subtypes.

pool_reachability.short: Which candidate pairs are reachable in the graph at all, and which are not.
pool_reachability.long: Reachability is the ceiling on recall: a target no path reaches cannot be ranked, however good the model is.

graph_nodes.short: Node identity, type, name and source for the whole graph. 22 recipes read it -- the index-to-entity lookup almost everything joins on.

graph_edges.short: Every edge in the assembled graph, with its relation. Feeds the matrix-form features computed outside Kuzu.

drug_disease_edges.short: Therapeutic-axis ground truth: indication and drug_investigated_for, kept as TWO relations.
drug_disease_edges.long: Only about 13% of Open Targets indication rows are approvals. Flattening the two relations into one would badly overstate approved evidence.

drug_protein_edges.short: Tractability-axis ground truth, and the only uninflated drug label in the project.

raw_disease_disease.short: The PRE-REVERSAL disease hierarchy. Assembly makes edges undirected, so hierarchy direction survives only here.
raw_disease_disease.long: This is the sole reason act 3's ontology indentation can be drawn: parent/child is unrecoverable from the assembled graph.

raw_ot_known_drug.short: Open Targets known-drug rows, the source of the curated drug labels.

disease_family_id.short: The disease-to-family mapping the grouped split groups on.

enriched_gene_druggability_v2.short: Druggability class per gene, derived from Open Targets tractability buckets.
enriched_gene_druggability_v2.long: Display annotation and a user-set filter only. Feeding it to the model was measured and rejected three times over.

enriched_gene_safety_v2.short: Safety liabilities per gene, from public flags.
enriched_gene_safety_v2.long: Display only. The discovery lift is measured against exactly these labels, so filtering on them makes the headline claim circular -- filtering the liability flag deletes ERBB2 from its own disease's list.

psplit_train_set.short: The training half of the grouped split, one row per candidate pair with all feature columns.
psplit_train_set.long: Sample it rather than reading it whole: the full 2.19M x 31 frame plus a correlation matrix gets OOM-killed. A 25% sample resolves null rates to ~0.1pp.

enriched_graph_features_candidate_psplit.short: The assembled per-pair feature table the model trains and scores on.

scored_champion.short: Champion m7-f14 scores over the validation population. The most upstream dataset the assertion scripts recompute from.

enriched_dwpc_GGD.short: Degree-weighted path count reaching the disease through an interacting gene. A champion feature.

enriched_dwpc_GPGD.short: Degree-weighted path count reaching the disease through a shared pathway. A champion feature.

enriched_dwpc_GCD.short: Degree-weighted path count reaching the disease through a shared drug. NOT a champion input.
